knowledge:
- key_parameters: type=Specifies the output data type to retrieve ("individuals", "biosamples", "analyses", "filtering_terms", "counts", "g_variants", "cnv_fraction", "cnv_frequency") ;; output=Specifies the output format, such as "pgxseg" or "seg" for variants, and "pgxfreq" or "pgxmatrix" for CNV frequencies ;; filters=Identifiers (e.g., NCIt codes) used to filter queries, combined with AND logic for metadata and OR logic for counts/frequencies ;; codematches=Logical value; if TRUE, excludes child concepts of hierarchical filters to return exact matches only ;; domain=Specifies the database domain, defaulting to "progenetix.org" but can be set to "cancercelllines.org" ;; save_file=Logical; when TRUE (only for type="g_variants"), saves retrieved variants to a local file instead of returning them ;; group_id=Column name used for grouping in survival plots or CNV frequency calculations
- alternatives: byconaut=An R package mentioned for local visualization of `.pgxseg` files when dealing with a large number of samples ;; IGV=An external tool mentioned for visualizing `.seg` files ;; Progenetix website=An online platform where users can upload `.pgxseg` files for visualization
- when_to_use: Use when retrieving curated cancer CNV profiles and clinical metadata from Progenetix or Cancer Cell Lines databases, analyzing copy number variation fractions/frequencies across cohorts, or processing and visualizing local copy number segment data
- pitfalls: Variant data (type="g_variants") cannot be queried using filters or individual IDs due to timeout constraints and must be queried using biosample IDs ;; codematches should not be set to TRUE when filters include ontology-irrelevant terms like PubMed or cohort identifiers ;; codematches is not available when type="analyses" because analysis data does not include filter information ;; Not all individuals or samples have available survival data, which may affect survival visualization ;; One biosample ID may correspond to multiple analysis IDs, meaning the number of analysis profiles may not equal the number of samples

workflows.name: process_local_pgxseg
workflows.intent: Extract segment data, metadata, calculate CNV frequencies, and visualize survival data from a local `.pgxseg` file.
input: example.pgxseg (A local tab-separated file containing copy number segment variants and associated clinical metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Extract segment data using pgxSegprocess ;; 2. Extract metadata using pgxSegprocess ;; 3. Visualize survival data using Kaplan-Meier plots ;; 4. Calculate CNV frequency based on metadata grouping ;; 5. Extract all data types simultaneously
workflows.code:
library(pgxRpi)
library(GenomicRanges)
file_name <- system.file("extdata", "example.pgxseg",package = 'pgxRpi')
seg <- pgxSegprocess(file=file_name,return_seg = TRUE)
meta <- pgxSegprocess(file=file_name,return_metadata = TRUE)
pgxSegprocess(file=file_name,show_KM_plot = TRUE)
pgxSegprocess(file=file_name,show_KM_plot = TRUE,group_id = 'histological_diagnosis_id')
pgxSegprocess(file=file_name,show_KM_plot = TRUE,pval=TRUE,palette='npg')
frequency <- pgxSegprocess(file=file_name,return_frequency = TRUE)
frequency_2 <- pgxSegprocess(file=file_name,return_frequency = TRUE, group_id ='icdo_morphology_id')
info <- pgxSegprocess(file=file_name,show_KM_plot = TRUE, return_seg = TRUE, return_metadata = TRUE, return_frequency = TRUE)

workflows.name: calculate_cnv_frequency
workflows.intent: Compute binned CNV frequencies from custom segment data.
input: segdata.tsv (A data frame or file containing segment data with sample ID, chromosome, start, end, and CNV state columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate CNV frequency using segtoFreq specifying the CNV state column index ;; 2. Calculate level-specific CNV frequency using EFO codes
workflows.code:
library(pgxRpi)
variants <- pgxLoader(type="g_variants",biosample_id = c("pgxbs-kftvhmz9", "pgxbs-kftvhnqz","pgxbs-kftvhupd"),output="pgxseg")
segdata <- variants[variants$variant_type %in% c("DUP","DEL"),]
segfreq1 <- segtoFreq(segdata,cnv_column_idx = 6, cohort_name="c1")
segfreq2 <- segtoFreq(segdata,cnv_column_idx = 9,cohort_name="c1")
